newsitem.title: UK: UK may seek to lift EU beef ban for N.Ireland - FT.
newsitem.headline: UK may seek to lift EU beef ban for N.Ireland - FT.

text.p: Britain's agriculture minister hopes to win exemption for Northern Ireland as the first step in lifting a European Union ban on British beef exports, the Financial Times said on Thursday.

The EU imposed the ban in March 1996 after scientists identified a human equivalent of bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE or 'Mad Cow Disease'). Scientists said eating infected beef products was the likely cause of the human illness.
British Agriculture Minister Jack Cunningham told the Financial Times that the ban was unlikely to be lifted in one go. "We'll have to salami-slice it away," he said.

Cunningham said the British province of Northern Ireland had a "powerful case" for an early lifting of the ban for beef from herds certified free of BSE. Northern Ireland has a very low incidence of the disease and a computerised cattle base to trace animal movements.
But the report noted that Cunningham's plan might bring him into conflict with ministerial colleagues representing Scotland and Wales, which both have strong farming lobbies.
The report said some officials believed the ban could be lifted in Northern Ireland within 12 months although Cunningham would not be drawn on timing.
